source_material: Full 2026 BMC Psychology accepted manuscript / article-in-press PDF
Published participant, design, blinding, analysis and outcome sections

study_assessment.notes: Custom study-level appraisal complementing result-specific RoB 2. Random allocation is stated but sequence generation/concealment are not described; assessor/analyst masking and objective outcome measurement are strong; missing data are handled with multiple imputation under an unverified MAR assumption; no prospective registry/SAP was identified. This is not a validated external quality score.

domains.supporting_text: Ninety-three eligible children were described as randomly allocated 31 per group, but the report does not describe sequence generation or allocation concealment.
Research assistants conducting pre-, post- and follow-up assessments were separate from intervention delivery and unaware of group assignment; primary data analysts were also blinded.
All 93 randomized participants were included using 20-fold multiple imputation. Little's MCAR test was significant and imputation assumed MAR without a reported MNAR sensitivity analysis.
Prospective memory was measured with a standardized computerized dual-task paradigm at pre-, post- and six-month follow-up by blinded assessment staff.
The article specifies its LMM, covariate, covariance, Rubin-pooling and multiplicity procedures, but no prospective trial registration or preserved statistical-analysis plan was identified.

result_assessments.estimand_or_result_scope: Effect of randomized group assignment on post-training prospective-memory performance in the CT/BT/control design.
result_assessments.notes: Outcome-scoped RoB 2 appraisal. Stage 5 has no approved contrast because the earlier rapid seed did not safely normalize one; this appraisal does not silently rewrite Stage 5. D1 is some concerns because randomization is stated without sequence/concealment detail. D3 is some concerns because MI assumes MAR after MCAR was rejected. D5 is some concerns because no prospective registry/SAP was identified.

result_assessments.estimand_or_result_scope: Effect of randomized group assignment on six-month prospective-memory performance in the CT/BT/control design.
result_assessments.notes: Delayed outcome-scoped RoB 2 appraisal. D1 and D5 share the trial-level concerns of the post-training result. D3 remains some concerns because the six-month result relies on multiple imputation under MAR after MCAR was rejected, with no reported sensitivity analysis for departures from MAR.

domains.domain_label: Bias arising from the randomization process
domains.supporting_text: The report states random allocation of 93 children, 31 per group, but does not describe sequence generation or allocation concealment.

domains.domain_label: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domains.supporting_text: Follow-up assessment staff and primary analysts were blinded; no systematic trial-context deviations from randomized assignment were identified.

domains.domain_label: Bias due to missing outcome data
domains.supporting_text: The six-month analysis included all randomized participants through multiple imputation, but MCAR was rejected and the MAR assumption was not stress-tested with a reported sensitivity analysis; delayed missingness is therefore not demonstrably ignorable.

domains.domain_label: Bias in measurement of the outcome
domains.supporting_text: Six-month prospective memory replicated the standardized computerized assessment procedure and was administered by staff blinded to randomized group.

domains.domain_label: Bias in selection of the reported result
domains.supporting_text: The six-month timepoint is explicitly described in the report, but without a prospective registry/SAP selection among eligible outcomes, metrics and analyses cannot be ruled out.
